steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (170 degrees C).
Place crackers to cover bottom of a 10x15-inch baking pan.
Combine sugar, butter, and cream of tartar in a saucepan; heat to a boil. Add pecans; pour mixture over crackers.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes. Cool in the pan about 3 minutes; remove from pan while still warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Pecan Praline Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This recipe may be simple, but the results are out of this world! Just top graham crackers with a mixture of brown sugar and pecans.
raw_recipe.name: Pecan Praline Cookies

review.reviewBody:
I finally manage to scoop this recipe from my aunt to compare with this recipe since a few of the reviews scared me. The recipes are identical except an explicit statement that says: DO NOT BOIL the mix but simply heat and stir until brown sugar is completely dissolved and to let it cool for about 10 minutes before pouring slowly over the graham crackers. This is a little time consuming but definately worth it in the end! Mine turned out just as anuty has always made them :)
Update: Apologies, I didnt look at the pan size, my cookie sheet is roughly 12x16 and fits 35 crackers perfectly.
This recipe is awesome and so easy. The key is to not boil the butter and sugar too long. As soon as it starts to boil, mix in your pecans and pour on top of graham crackers.
I only used 1/2 butter and I didn't have any cream of tartar, but they turned out great! I could only fit 25 crackers on my biggest sheet, they were great!

Made this today! Used ~9x13 cookie sheet, which I lined with heavy duty foil and sprayed with buttery Pam then wiped off excess. Followed recipe using light brown sugar, stirring constantly, added 1tsp vanilla and turned heat down to low as soon as mixture started bubbling. Did not add pecans to syrup- spread thin layer of syrup over crackers, sprinkled pecans on, then drizzled rest of syrup over the top. Baked for 10 mins, let sit 10 mins before moving foil to cutting board to cool. Waited until firm before breaking into serving pieces.

The trick to this recipe is using silicone or baking paper....I use a Silpat lining the cookie sheet. boil the sugar/butter mixture for at least 3 minutes at a full boil. I stir in the nuts just before I pour the butter/sugar mix over the graham crackers. 

Bake at 350 for 10 to 12 minutes and take them out and let them sit for at least an hour. The whole mass will slide off the Silpat onto sheets of wax paper and then you can break them up. At this point, I use melted chocolate chips with parafin melted in the chocolate to make it harden. I drizzle the chocolate/parafin mix over the top of the crackers to make it absolutely delicious. 

Once that dries, in a couple of hours, then simply break apart and store between sheets of wax paper in a tin in the fridge. If they last long enough to store them!!!!

We love these! I like to add a sprinkle of chocolate chips after I take them out of the oven. A great clean up saver: use parchment paper to line the cookie sheet. After it cools on the pan for a minute, you can then remove the whole sheet and put on the counter to finish cooling. I then put it in the refrigerator for 5-10 minutes.

Great, great cookies with a fantastic flavor and crunchiness. And, so easy to make! I tried baking the cookies last week. Following the recipe exactly as was provided, I found the cookies too sweet and too greasy. But when I brought a batch to work, my colleagues (mostly women !!) loved them.
Still, I wanted cookies that are less sweet and greasy. So I baked the cookies again a few days later, using 3/4 cup of butter and 3/4 cup of brown sugar. I also chopped the pecans into tiny pieces and adjust baking time to 9 minutes. The result was exactly as I wanted: there was enough liquid mixture to cover all the graham crackers, good distribution of pecans, sweet enough cookies, less greasy and super crunchy.
My colleagues all agreed the second batch was better and actually just amazing!
Thank you for a great recipe. It will be a keeper!

I have used a similar recipe for years (mine does not call for cream of tartar, but uses butter AND margarine with the light brown sugar). I boil my butter/sugar mixture for about 2 minutes (stirring constantly) until it looks bubbly. I do not put the pecans in the mixture because they get lost in the liquid and are not evenly spread over the crackers (some crackers will have a lot and others will have none). I sprinkle them on the crackers and then carefully ladle the sugar mixture over the crackers. The mixture will seep under the crackers, but if the crackers are floating in it, you have way too much. I just try to make sure the pecans and the tops of the crackers are coated with the butter/sugar mixture and I often have some of the mixture left over that I use on my next pan of pecan cookies. Then I bake them approx. 10 mins until the crackers look bubbly in the pan. It will harden as it cools, but I use a pizza cutter to roll between each cracker while they are still warm. Otherwise, it is difficult to cut them apart.

I have made these several times and have actually had people kiss my feet when I served them. For people who have had problems, this is what I do and they always turn out great. Make sure the cookies lay flat in the pan - don't stack them. I use 12 full graham crackers, broken in half (24 halves) and they fit the pan perfectly. Bring the ingredients to a light boil, stirring contantly. As soon as the butter and brown sugar form a homogenous syrup, take them off the heat, add pecans (I also add some vanilla here), pour over graham crackers. It should JUST cover the graham crackers, you may need to spread it with a spoon. Immediately put in oven and bake on NONSTICK pan. Let them cool until they come off in one piece, but no longer. Put on foil to cool COMPLETELY and harden before eating.

It is very good. I was going to add pecans as the nuts but I saw "Pecan Lover's" Planters nuts (pecans, cashews and pistachios) and thought I would give that a try. Ground them up in the blender. Boiled the butter sugar for 3 minutes. and baked for 20 minutes. Probably 5 minutes too long but there was pooled butter on my crackers at the end of 10 minutes. I used Honeymaid Honey grahams and got 15 (3x5)whole crackers (not broken into 4) on a low lip sheet pan. Yummy

I'm rating this based on looks alone. I just took my stuff out of the oven and they look PERFECT. My mom has made these before, so I know what they taste like. I followed this recipe - not sure what her recipe is like. I didn't mix in pecans - simply because they're really not my favorite. Instead, I sprinkled the top (before baking) with sliced almonds. They look beautiful. I also lined my cookie sheet with parchment paper. Both cleanup and cutting should be a cinch. I was worried that I would have sogginess or pooling butter or other problems that people had. I melted my butter and brown sugar on medium heat until the butter had melted (I kept stirring it during this time). Then I turned it on high until it came to a boil. I could tell the syrup was ready because it coated my spatula. I think that's the best way to test it. When it coats your silicone spoon/spatula. Before I boiled it, the butter wouldn't even let it stick to my spatula. So I could tell once the butter and sugar came together by the sticking. Anyway. It worked for me! I'm very excited to try it!

Loved this recipe I used dark brown sugar instead of the light brown sugar will definitely make this again the only thing different i will next time is add some maple flavor to it I think that will be divine
My man loved them!

I make this every year everyone loves it, I didn't use the tarter, used vanilla instead cause that's what my old recipe called for also didn't call for baking it either just poured mixture straight on crackers and nuts and freezer it if you have a big enough flat area in a deep freezer. Tried it a few ways all seem to turn out about the same. Might have to try tarter sometime
We have made these cookies for years. I always place a copy of the recipe with the cookies when I give them because every person who has received them asks for it.
This is very simple to make yet the results are SCRUMPTIOUS! I used Shar Gluten-free Graham Crackers and they came out GREAT!

This was a crowd pleaser. It's very easy & doesn't involve shopping for a bunch of ingredients. YOU MUST LET MIXTURE COOL FOR 10 MINUTES BEFORE POURING MIXTURE ON GRAHAM CRACKERS. Thank you to the reviewer that called this out. This is important. As suggested by others, I didn't boil but let simmer for just a few minutes. Good luck!
I made it and it was just o.k. The crust was very buttery - almost greasy. It was good, but I wouldn't write any raves over it.
Light brown sugar and run makes them special. If you use dark brown sugar, then it's a more toasty flavor. Both work perfectly well.
Awesome! Making again.
